confidence: high (identity gap), medium (retarget race requires timing)
user_consequence: A player who decides to tap the calendar's single 'Respond' primary action cannot see, at the moment of deciding, which event it will open — the button carries no event title/date. If a background realtime notification (any golf_events row change on the team, not necessarily this event) lands and triggers router.refresh()+refetchVisibleRange() between the player's decision to tap and the actual pointerup, React will have already swapped the onClick handler to point at whatever event is now 'most imminent un-RSVP'd' before the click fires — so the player can open, and RSVP to, a different event than the one they meant to respond to, with no on-screen warning that the target changed.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx's `mostImminentUnrsvpd` (a useMemo over `events`/`serverNow`/`userRsvpStatuses`) feeds `handlePrimaryAction` (a useCallback that closes over it) which is passed to FairwayCalendarHero as `onPrimaryAction`. `events` itself is `useCalendarRangeEvents(...).events`, which is intentionally live-updated by the realtime channel's `onRealtimeEvent: () => router.refresh()` and by every `postgres_changes` event on `golf_events` for the team (use-calendar-range-events.ts:502-545) — not scoped to the specific event being displayed. Because React always uses the onClick prop current at click time, not the one visible when the user last read the label, any re-render between decision and tap silently retargets the button. FairwayCalendarHero.tsx never renders the target event's title/date next to the 'Respond' label (only the isCoach ? 'New event' : 'Respond' static string), so there is no way for the player to notice, even after the fact, that the button just changed meaning.
expected: Section 7's Calendar interaction contract: 'Named event-bound RSVP... Reject the design when... a global Respond button silently changes target.'
actual: Respond is bound to a named event id at click time (not a truly global button), but the id it is bound to can change between the last paint the user saw and the actual click, and the button never displays which event it targets.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: render the target event's title/date inline on or beside the primary action ('Respond to Practice — Thu 4:00 PM') so a retarget is visible before the tap; and/or freeze `mostImminentUnrsvpd` for the duration of a user gesture (e.g. snapshot on pointerdown, or debounce the realtime-triggered recompute while a press is in flight) so a background refresh cannot change the committed target mid-gesture. Reuse the existing FairwayCalendarHero composition and A03 Button/typography tokens — no new primitive.
accessibility_check: NOT_RUN — requires a screen reader session to confirm the retarget is also silent to VoiceOver users (aria-label on the Button is just 'Respond', no event identity either).

user_consequence: If an event is cancelled, rescheduled, or has its RSVP deadline changed by a coach (or by a realtime-triggered refresh) WHILE a player already has that event's detail drawer open, the drawer keeps showing the stale pre-change state: RSVP buttons stay live and unlocked for what is now a cancelled event or a passed deadline. Tapping 'Going'/'Maybe'/'Decline' still submits — the write is correctly rejected server-side (RSVPLockedError) and surfaces as an error string via `rsvpLockMessage`, so no wrong data is persisted, but the player experiences a confusing 'looked fine, then errored' interaction instead of the drawer proactively showing the new locked/cancelled state. The same staleness applies to a coach's edit editor: `editorEvent` is a point-in-time snapshot.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx holds `drawerEvent`/`editorEvent` as component state, set exactly once in `openDrawerForEvent(event)` / `openEdit(ev)` and cleared only when the sheet closes (drawerEvent additionally cleared via a 240ms setTimeout after close). No effect re-syncs either from the live, realtime-updated `events` array (the same array `mostImminentUnrsvpd` and the day-strip/agenda/month bodies all read from) while the sheet is open. `FairwayEventDetailDrawer`'s lock computation (`isCancelled`, `hasStarted`, `deadlinePassed`, `rsvpLocked`) is derived entirely from the `event` prop it was handed, so it is only ever as fresh as the moment the drawer opened. The same snapshot problem applies to `FairwayEventEditor`'s recurring edit-scope math: `editRecurringEvent`'s `originalStartDate` (used to bound the 'thisAndFuture' scope's row filter, src/app/golf/actions/recurring-events.ts:1227) is `editorEvent.start_date` captured at open time — if a concurrent edit has already moved that occurrence's date by the time the coach saves, the 'future' boundary is computed from a stale anchor date.
expected: Section 9.2's mutation truth table + Section 6 A07 order: 'Check deadlines/locks, cancelation, occurrence edits and permission changes while details are open.'
actual: The drawer/editor never observes a change to the entity it is displaying once open; only the eventual write attempt discovers the new server truth.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: derive `drawerEvent`/`editorEvent` by id-lookup into the live `events` array on every render (`events.find(e => e.id === openId) ?? lastKnownSnapshot`) instead of freezing the object at open time, so a cancellation/reschedule while the sheet is open is reflected live; when the live lookup returns null (hard-deleted while open), show an explicit 'This event was removed' state rather than silently keeping the stale copy. For the recurring edit-scope case, re-derive `originalStartDate` from the live event at submit time rather than at editor-open time.

user_consequence: Navigating (Agenda/Week/Month) to a date range the client hasn't fetched yet can show 'No upcoming events' / 'Nothing upcoming — check back when your coach adds events' at the exact same moment a 'Loading events for this date range…' banner sits above it — the confirmed-empty message and the still-loading message render together, so the user cannot tell whether the calendar is actually empty there or simply hasn't finished asking yet.
mechanism: `FairwayCalendar` renders `isLoadingRange`/`rangeError` only as an inline banner (FairwayCalendar.tsx:1038-1062) directly above the body, but the body components themselves (`FairwayAgendaView`, and by the same pattern `FairwayMonthGrid`) never receive `isLoadingRange` as a prop — their honest-empty branch is gated purely on `totalEvents === 0` (FairwayAgendaView.tsx:236-257 for range mode, :260-285 for day mode), computed from whatever `events` the range hook currently holds. Per `useCalendarRangeEvents` (use-calendar-range-events.ts:336-479), a not-yet-covered range genuinely has zero matching rows in `eventVersions` until its fetch resolves, so the empty state renders immediately and only clears (or doesn't) once the fetch lands — 'zero events' and 'haven't asked yet' are indistinguishable to the body while `isLoadingRange` is true.
expected: Section 9.1: 'New scope without matching result → Stable controls; dependent-region placeholder' and Section 7 Calendar reject-condition: 'empty equals unqueried.'
actual: The honest-empty state and the in-flight loading banner can both be on screen at once for the same navigation, with the empty state written in confirmed-empty language ('Check back when your coach adds events').
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: thread `isLoadingRange` into `FairwayAgendaView`/`FairwayMonthGrid` and render a neutral loading placeholder (skeleton rows, or simply suppress the EmptyState copy) instead of the confirmed-empty state while the exact visible range is still being fetched. Keep the existing banner and the existing beneficial streaming/error handling unchanged — this is additive gating, not a replacement.

user_consequence: On a multi-day event (a tournament, a multi-day trip), the week's day-strip shows a density dot only under the FIRST day of the event; every subsequent day the event actually runs shows no dot and its accessible label reads '— no events', even though the Month grid and the Agenda list directly below correctly show the same event live on those days. A player or coach scanning the day-strip for 'what's happening this week' undercounts multi-day commitments exactly on the days that matter (day 2+ of a tournament).
mechanism: `FairwayDayStrip`'s density-dot bucketing keys events by `zonedDayKey(ev.start_date || ev.start_time, teamTimezone)` — the event's START instant only (FairwayDayStrip.tsx:110-121) — while every other calendar surface in this same file family (`FairwayMonthGrid.tsx:151`, `FairwayAgendaView.tsx:89,126`) explicitly uses `eventDaySpan` from `src/lib/calendar/timezone.ts`, whose own doc comment (timezone.ts:191-208) documents that reading only the start day is precisely the bug class already found and fixed on production ('#1493/#1494/#1495/#1496... all 14 multi-day events... invisible after their first day'). The day-strip is the one caller in this component family that was never updated to the eventDaySpan convention.
expected: eventRunsOnDay/eventDaySpan is the canonical, already-battle-tested rule for 'does this event occupy this calendar day' used consistently by Month and Agenda.
actual: FairwayDayStrip computes day membership independently via start-day-only bucketing, silently disagreeing with the body it sits directly above.
proposed_fix: SOURCE fix, low risk: replace `zonedDayKey`-based bucketing in `eventsByDay` with a pass that calls `eventRunsOnDay(ev, teamTimezone, dayKey)` (or `eventDaySpan` + an inclusive-range membership test, matching FairwayAgendaView's day-mode filter at FairwayAgendaView.tsx:86-99) for each of the 7 visible days, so a multi-day event contributes a dot to every day it actually runs, matching the Month/Agenda bodies.
accessibility_check: aria-label on each day pill says '— no events' for days a multi-day event is actually running; a VoiceOver user relying on the label is told the day is free when it isn't.

user_consequence: The hero's honest status line ('N upcoming · M this week/month/in view') can under-report relative to what the body directly below it actually shows: a multi-day event that started before the visible window but is still running inside it (e.g., a Friday-start tournament viewed from the following Monday's week) is rendered by the Agenda/Month body (which correctly uses eventDaySpan overlap) but not counted in `windowCount`, which only tests whether the event's START timestamp falls inside the window.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx's `windowCount` useMemo (lines 723-751) has two branches: the `view === 'day'` branch correctly uses `eventDaySpan` overlap (matching the body), but the week/month/agenda branch (lines 743-750) filters solely on `new Date(e.start_time || e.start_date).getTime()` against `[visibleWindow.start, visibleWindow.end]` — a pure start-timestamp test with no span/overlap logic. Meanwhile the body rendered below (`FairwayAgendaView` range mode, `FairwayMonthGrid`) both use `eventDaySpan` and render the event on every day of its span that falls in the window, including when its start is before the window.
expected: Section 6 A07 order: 'Counts such as upcoming/in-view/earlier need exact set definitions' consistent with what the same screen's body displays.
actual: windowCount (in-view count) and the body's actual visible-event set use two different set definitions for week/month/agenda views (start-only vs. span-overlap); they only agree for the day view.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: define `windowCount` for every view via the same span-overlap test the day-view branch and the bodies already use (`eventDaySpan` overlap against `[visibleWindow.start, visibleWindow.end]`), not start-timestamp membership, so the header count and the rendered list are always counting the same set.

user_consequence: A player's Home 'Today' card can show the next event's time computed in the WRONG timezone whenever the team has no timezone configured (a real, already-documented state — the calendar page itself computes `teamTimezone = teamSettingsResult.data?.timezone || null`): the server render (Vercel, UTC) and the first client render (the player's own browser zone, e.g. America/New_York) can print two different times for the identical event, a ~4-5h discrepancy depending on which pass the player actually reads — the exact defect class this codebase has already found and fixed once, elsewhere.
mechanism: `src/components/fairway/pages/dashboard/player-dashboard-parts.tsx:104-114` defines its own local `formatEventTime(start, timezone?)` using `new Date(start).toLocaleTimeString('en-US', { timeZone: timezone })`. Its sole caller, `FairwayPlayerDashboard.tsx:710`, passes `timezone={enhancedData?.timezone}` — optional-chained, so it is `undefined` whenever the team timezone lookup is null. `Intl`/`toLocaleTimeString` with `timeZone: undefined` resolves to the RUNTIME's own local zone, which differs between the Vercel server process (UTC) and the browser. The canonical `formatEventTime` in `src/lib/calendar/timezone.ts:81-90` was written specifically to fix this exact class of bug (its own comment cites 'audit W1... times shift ~4h... tripped React #418') by always falling back to `DEFAULT_TIMEZONE` via `getValidTimezone` rather than the ambient runtime zone — the Home-card's local fork re-implements the same idea without that fallback, reopening the fixed defect on one surface. Confirmed as flagged independently by A04; recorded here because I own the shared calendar-timezone semantics this fork should be using.
expected: One canonical event-time formatter (src/lib/calendar/timezone.ts's formatEventTime) used everywhere an event's wall-clock time is rendered, so SSR and CSR always agree regardless of whether a team timezone is configured.
actual: A second, independent implementation exists on the player Home card with no DEFAULT_TIMEZONE fallback.
proposed_fix: SHARED CHANGE REQUEST to A04 (owns Home/player-dashboard-parts.tsx): delete the local `formatEventTime` in player-dashboard-parts.tsx and import `formatEventTime` from `@/lib/calendar/timezone` instead — same call signature (iso, timezone), already handles the null/invalid-timezone fallback correctly. I am not editing this file directly per the A04 boundary; recording the exact change here so it can land as a one-line import swap.
owner_lane: A04 (shared calendar-timezone semantics owned by A07)

user_consequence: A cross-link into the calendar for a specific event (`?event=<id>`, currently used by the Travel→Calendar 'Linked calendar event' chip) that points at an event outside the loaded/visible range, already deleted, or on the wrong team silently drops the user on the generic calendar hub with no indication their deep link resolved to nothing — no error, no toast, no 'that event isn't available' message.
mechanism: FairwayCalendar.tsx:880-887's auto-open effect only checks membership in the already-loaded `events` array (server ±3-month window plus whatever ranges the client has since fetched by navigation) — `const match = events.find((e) => e.id === initialEventId); if (!match) return;` — there is no dedicated fetch-by-id fallback for a linked event outside every range the user happens to have loaded.
expected: Section 6 A07 order: 'Deep links to missing/out-of-range events need a targeted authorized fetch or explicit unavailability, not a silent generic calendar.'
actual: A deep link to an out-of-range/deleted/wrong-team event is indistinguishable, to the user, from simply landing on the calendar with no query param at all.
proposed_fix: PROPOSAL: when `initialEventId` is present and not found in the loaded `events` after the initial load settles, issue one targeted `getEvent(id)`-style fetch (respecting RLS); on success, jump focus to that date and open the drawer; on a genuine miss/denial, surface an explicit 'This event is no longer available' toast/banner rather than silence.
